TERMINAL DELIGHT · OPS · 22 OCTOBER 2026

Ops Glass

Ops is one of Terminal Delight’s window styles. Your screenshots showed the same sharp grid in its overlay panels and its left navigation spine. You asked for smoked glass, with the desktop behind the overlay groupings and the grid behind the spine.

measured · native capturesmeasured · 2,716 tests passed

Under the Smoke

The existing overlay plate covered the terminals with an opaque background. Making its smaller groupings translucent would only reveal that plate. Exposing the desktop required removing the pixels beneath each grouping.

Desktop Cutouts

I added a drawing operation that replaces those pixels with a translucent face. Its controls paint afterward, so they remain sharp. The native capture below records the resulting openings as real transparency.

Grid Frost

That operation would also remove the grid beneath the left spine. The spine keeps an opaque backing and spreads its grid lines into soft bands before painting its labels. The softness therefore stops at the background.

Window Rules

The desktop openings also need the limits you specified. At full window opacity or in fullscreen, the grouping faces fill solid. An unavailable compositor reading keeps them solid as well.

On this Omarchy desktop, the app reads the compositor’s active and inactive opacity settings separately. The read uses Hyprland’s local socket. An unavailable setting, including on other compositors, keeps the face solid.

Native Checks

The next check was whether the shared material preserved controls in other overlays. The first gauges capture hid its sliders beneath a backing drawn last. I moved the backing ahead of the controls and captured it again. The corrected gauges and the bug reporter keep their controls above the glass.

The full regression suite then passed: 2,716 tests, with 15 existing tests ignored. Clippy passed on both terminal cores, and formatting passed. Native captures confirm transparent groupings, solid frame pixels and a solid spine with a softened grid. The opacity and fullscreen fallbacks passed policy tests; they have not been photographed separately.

The new build is ready. Reloading the running window waits for confirmation that the open lead-discovery document has no unsaved notes; the current guard cannot report its unsaved-note count.
